closesNoSectionSevenOneRow.statement: THIS REVIEW CLOSES NO IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 7.1 ROW, and none was edited.
closesNoSectionSevenOneRow.couldOneBeClosed: NO -- not by this artifact and not by this review, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of quality. The EvidenceDigest row cannot close while DUD-1 and DUD-2 stand: R-0 through R-4 transcribe from evaluation-proof.v8 and evidence.v10, and BOTH are CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED. operability.v10 parks the recipe with the words "do not yet exist as exact live byte contracts", and that park is about APPLICATION, which is a coordinator act at the Phase-1A insertion and not an authoring act. Independently of application, v3 itself establishes that five of SemanticEvidenceV1 thirteen field values have no recipe in the artifact and that one of them has no reproduced derivation anywhere by anyone -- so even a fully applied EP8 and evidence.v10 would leave the row short of an end-to-end computable identity. Closing it would require authoring a canonical-JSON profile, which is precisely the design act section 7.1 reserves.
closesNoSectionSevenOneRow.whatThisReviewDoesInstead: It records that the recipes reproduce, that the headline set-algebra claim is correct, and that three defects in the artifact own self-certification must be repaired before a successor is credible as a MEASURED document.

theSeventhEncoder.mandate: The dispatch brief required a SEVENTH independent encoder written from v3 prose alone.
theSeventhEncoder.whatWasWritten: A fresh Python module implementing sharedPrimitives (componentFrame, textComponent, canonicalUnsignedDecimal, typedScalarValueEncoding), R-0 TCMS-V5 steps 1-8, the MemberV1 / OutcomeV1 / SubjectV1 record grammars, R-1 thirteen-field SemanticEvidenceV1 table, RawProofInventoryV1 and ItemV1, and DomainEnvelopeV1. Python standard library only: hashlib, struct, unicodedata, re. It shares no line with v1, v2, v3, either review, the sweep, or any check-*.py, and it was written before any published digest was consulted.
theSeventhEncoder.result: ALL 32 PUBLISHED VECTORS REPRODUCE. 95 assertions run, 95 pass, 0 fail.
theSeventhEncoder.whatWasCoveredBeyondTheHeadlineDigests: Not only each expectedCommitment but also every published counter-digest (naive text sort, duplicate-last, no-bound-enforced, code-point counting, silent normalization), every published byte length (rawProofInventoryByteLength, semanticEvidenceByteLength, evidenceDigestPreimageByteLength, subjectV1RecordByteLength), the two ED-6 full preimage hexes, the BND-4 accepted record hex, and each REJECTION asserted BY ITS SPECIFIC CONDITION rather than by a non-zero exit.
theSeventhEncoder.rejectionsAssertedByName: SS-5 raised "duplicate exact record bytes"; BND-2 and BND-3 raised "text component exceeds 4096 bytes"; BND-4 and all three BND-5 singletons raised "text component is not NFC". A non-zero exit was never accepted as evidence a guard fired.
theSeventhEncoder.theINDEPENDENTGoldenReproduction: STRONGER THAN THE VECTOR SUITE, because it does not use v3 numbers at all. This reviewer rebuilt evidence.v10 acceptedGolden from evidence.v10 OWN acceptedGolden.values plus the const schemaVersion read off its own field declarations, taking only the 23 inventory items from v3 (the sole place they are published as logical values). rawProofInventoryHex, semanticEvidenceHex and evidenceDigestPreimageHex all matched BYTE-EXACTLY at 2836, 3560 and 3599 bytes, and both semanticEvidenceCasRef and evidenceDigest matched.
theSeventhEncoder.theNineEP8Goldens: ALL NINE REPRODUCED, 45 assertions, 0 fail -- sortedUniqueItemHex, leafHashHex, merkleRootHex, outerPreimageHex and commitment recomputed for each from the declared item bytes.
theSeventhEncoder.conclusion: SEVEN INDEPENDENT ENCODERS NOW AGREE ON EVERY PUBLISHED VALUE. This reviewer found no arithmetic defect, no framing defect and no digest disagreement anywhere in R-0 through R-4. The recipes are not where the defects are, and this is the third successive review to reach that conclusion.

blockers.title: v3 CONTAINS A JSON NUMBER, WHICH FALSIFIES THREE OF ITS OWN EXPLICIT SELF-CLAIMS, INCLUDING A MEASUREMENT IT REPORTS AS HAVING RUN
blockers.theMeasurement: A full recursive leaf walk of the live bytes of evidence-identity-recipes.v3.json returns 2225 leaves, of which 2224 are strings and ONE IS A JSON INTEGER. Its path is .repairOfBlockerOne.theRepair_STEP1_enumerateAgainstTheSourcesOwnTypeDeclarations.theThirteenFieldsClassified[0].declaredValue and its value is the bare token 1. It is on line 65 of the file and is visible to a raw byte grep for the exact string '"declaredValue": 1,'.
whatItFalsifies: numericRepresentationRule.rule, verbatim: "This artifact contains NO JSON number and NO JSON boolean and NO JSON null at any leaf, at any depth." FALSE as measured.

numericRepresentationRule.why, verbatim: "this artifact makes a JSON number UNEXPRESSIBLE in its own leaf space. A respelling attack needs a numeric position to occupy, and there is none." FALSE as measured -- there is exactly one, and it holds an integer constant.

numericRepresentationRule.measured, verbatim: "verified by a full recursive leaf walk of these exact bytes after writing; see measuredSelfReport." The walk either was not run on the emitted bytes or was run and its result misreported. Either way a MEASURED claim is untrue of the bytes it names.
blockers.itIsAREGRESSIONIntroducedByV3: MEASURED ACROSS THE LINEAGE. v1: 796 leaves, 0 non-strings. v2: 1381 leaves, 0 non-strings. v3: 2225 leaves, 1 integer. v3 is the FIRST artifact in this lineage to break the property -- and it is also the first to CLAIM it deliberately. numericRepresentationRule.nullIsNOWCLAIMEDToo says the property is "CLAIMED here on purpose, so that a successor cannot lose it silently". v3 then lost it silently, in its own bytes, in the same pass.
blockers.theMECHANISMAndWhyItMatters: The integer entered through the GENERATOR. measuredSelfReport.countsDerivedNotTyped states that the thirteen-field classification "was produced by programmatic walks over the live bytes and inserted into this file by the generator". The walk copied evidence.v10 field declaration {"name":"schemaVersion","tag":"0x90","const":1} and carried the const value across with its JSON TYPE intact, bypassing the string-only discipline. The defect therefore entered through the exact apparatus introduced to repair B-EIR2-01: automation removed a hand-transcription error class and introduced a type-fidelity error class, and the self-check that would have caught it is reported as having passed.
blockers.whyThisIsBLOCKINGAndNotCosmetic: FOUR REASONS, none of them stylistic. (1) The rule exists to defeat LB-C2-01, which v3 own why clause explains defeated C-2 at v3, v5, v6, v7 and v8 successively, EACH TIME INSIDE THE REPAIR OWN SELF-CERTIFICATION -- which is precisely what has happened again here. (2) The position that now holds a number is a schemaVersion const, i.e. the exact shape the rule names: "an integer constant compared with == accepts a float spelling of itself and hash(1.0) == hash(1)". A successor regenerating this table from a source that spells the const 1.0 would emit 1.0 here and no stated property of this file would forbid it. (3) The claim is not incidental prose; it is a declared structural property of THESE EXACT BYTES, offered as a guarantee to successors. (4) A document whose central methodological claim is "MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED" carries a false measured self-report. The corpus standard, which v3 states in its own bytes, is that a rule nothing can check is prose that looks like specification; a measurement reported but not true of the emitted bytes is worse.
blockers.whatWouldClearIt: Emit the declaredValue as the string "1" (the artifact already carries every other count and constant as a canonical ASCII decimal string, including wireBytes "0x31" and the schemaVersion "1" of every test vector), then re-run the leaf walk against the EMITTED bytes and publish the census. No recipe, digest, vector or disposition is affected.
blockers.whatItDoesNOTImpugn: NO DIGEST, NO VECTOR AND NO RECIPE. This reviewer seventh encoder reproduced all 32 vectors and all nine EP8 goldens with the integer present. The defect is in the self-certification, not the substance.

blockers.title: THE REPAIRED WARRANT FOR SILENTLY-DROPPED: 0 IS STILL NOT SOUND -- AN ENTIRE SECTION OF A NAMED SOURCE GRAMMAR IS OUTSIDE THE KEY SET, IS UNDECLARED, AND IS A SECTION THE ARTIFACT TRANSCRIBES FROM
blockers.whatV3Claims: theRepair_theMethodStatedHonestly.theNEWWarrantForSILENTLYDROPPEDZero, verbatim: "A clause can therefore be silently dropped only by being absent from the source key set itself, WHICH IS A PROPERTY OF THE SOURCES AND NOT OF THIS AUTHOR READING."
blockers.theMeasurement: MEASURED AGAINST LIVE BYTES. evaluation-proof.v8#normativePreimageGrammar has SEVEN top-level keys: id, namespaceUtf8, scalarEncoding, recordRules, records, commitment, domains. The swept set named in v3 own method sentence is {scalarEncoding, recordRules, commitment, domains}. Excluded, therefore, are id, namespaceUtf8 and -- decisively -- records, a list of ELEVEN record grammars (MemberV1, OutcomeV1, WaiverV1, SubjectV1, BaselineV1, PolicyV2, VerdictInputV2, ActivationManifestV1, ActivationMemberV1, EvaluationAuthoritySealV1, SemanticObjectBindingV1) carrying recordTag, fields, order, forbiddenFields and variantRule.
blockers.theASYMMETRYThatMakesItAnOversightRather: evidence.v10#canonicalWireGrammar has SEVEN top-level keys and v3 sweeps SIX of them, excluding only id. Its records section IS swept, contributing five keys. So the same-named section is IN scope on source B and OUT of scope on source A, with no reason given for the difference. v3 emphasises that it widened source B scope to six sections by adding tagRegistry; it did not perform the corresponding widening on source A.
blockers.whyItIsNotDeclared: TWO PLACES WHERE IT SHOULD APPEAR AND DOES NOT. (1) theTwoKeysGivenNOROW names exactly two keys given no row, ccg.version and ccg.domains; npg.records is not a key given no row, it is a section outside the key set entirely. (2) result.boundsOfThisSweep, verbatim, says the sweep "covers the two source GRAMMARS and nothing else" and then lists what it does not sweep: "evidence.v10 invariants, retainedResiduals, adversarialControls or evidenceRecomputationContract, nor evaluation-proof.v8 invariants, collisionControls, adversarialControls or its twelve authority sections." EVERY EXCLUSION NAMED THERE IS A SIBLING OF THE GRAMMARS. A section INSIDE a grammar the sweep claims to cover in full is named nowhere.
blockers.whyItIsMATERIALAndNotPedantic: R-0 TRANSCRIBES FROM THE UNSWEPT SECTION AND SAYS SO THREE TIMES. R-0-typedComponentMerkleSet.recordGrammars.MemberV1.source, .OutcomeV1.source and .SubjectV1.source each read "evaluation-proof.v8#normativePreimageGrammar.records[...]". The clause-level sweep whose output is SILENTLY-DROPPED: 0 therefore does not cover the source of three of the artifact own record grammars. A dropped clause in MemberV1, OutcomeV1 or SubjectV1 -- a forbiddenFields entry, an order constraint, a variantRule -- is invisible to this sweep by construction.
blockers.theSENTENCEIsFalseAsWritten: Absence from the 56-key set is NOT "a property of the sources". The 56 keys are the direct children of ELEVEN AUTHOR-CHOSEN SECTIONS. v3 correctly abandoned v2 false claim that the clause list was "the source own key set"; the replacement warrant reintroduces the same move one level up, relocating the unexamined author choice from the CLAUSE decomposition to the SECTION selection.
blockers.whatThisReviewerDIDVerifyInMitigation: NO CLAUSE WAS ACTUALLY LOST IN A DIGEST-AFFECTING WAY. This reviewer checked the three transcribed grammars directly against evaluation-proof.v8 live bytes -- MemberV1 recordTag 0x10 with 2 fields, OutcomeV1 0x11 with 3, SubjectV1 0x13 with 1 -- and all three match R-0 transcription exactly. The seventh encoder then reproduced all nine EP8 commitment goldens, which exercise those grammars end to end. THE DEFECT IS IN THE WARRANT, NOT IN THE TRANSCRIPTION. That is why it is filed as a blocker on a certification claim rather than as a correctness defect in a recipe.
blockers.whatWouldClearIt: Either extend the key set to normativePreimageGrammar.records and publish the resulting rows, or name the exclusion explicitly in boundsOfThisSweep alongside the sibling exclusions and restate the warrant as a claim about the ELEVEN CHOSEN SECTIONS rather than about the sources. The second is a one-sentence repair and is sufficient.

blockers.title: THE PUBLISHED AUDIT SHORTCUT NAMES THREE COLLAPSES WHERE FOUR EXIST, CONTRADICTS THE ARTIFACT OWN ARITHMETIC, AND ASSERTS ITS OWN COMPLETENESS WHILE DOING SO
blockers.theMeasurement: Counting entries with relation == "COLLAPSE" across both derivation tables in transcriptionFidelitySweep.keyToRowDerivation returns FOUR, not three: one on source A (canonicalCommitmentGrammar.{leaf, internal, oddNode, emptySet, outer}, 5 keys into 1 row) and THREE on source B (canonicalWireGrammar.scalarEncoding.{componentFrame, blobFrame} 2 into 1; canonicalWireGrammar.domainEnvelope.{recordTag, fields, encoding} 3 into 1; and canonicalWireGrammar.records.{RunIdentityPreimageV1, TerminalRunV1} 2 into 1). The list theTHREECollapsesAReviewerShouldCheckFirst names the first three and OMITS THE FOURTH.
blockers.itContradictsTheArtifactOwnArithmetic: arithmeticSourceB, verbatim: "23 keys, minus 1 absorbed by the componentFrame/blobFrame collapse, minus 2 by the domainEnvelope collapse, MINUS 1 BY THE RunIdentityPreimageV1/TerminalRunV1 COLLAPSE, plus 4 from the text split, plus 2 from the decoding split = 25." The omitted collapse is named there, in the same section, as a load-bearing term. The artifact counts four and lists three.
blockers.theSelfReferentialPart: The third listed item carries the note, verbatim: "it is a THIRD multi-key collapse IN A LIST THAT CLAIMED TO BE COMPLETE, which is the same failure class one level down." It is the third of FOUR. The sentence diagnosing an incomplete list is itself an entry in an incomplete list, and the ordinal it asserts is wrong.
blockers.theCONCRETEHarmToAReviewer: THIS IS NOT AN UNUSED ORNAMENT -- IT IS THE AUDIT PATH v3 INSTRUCTS A REVIEWER TO WALK. result-side text whatTheZeroSTILLDoesNotCover, verbatim: "every SPLIT and every COLLAPSE is named below with its clause count, so a reviewer can GO STRAIGHT TO THE THREE COLLAPSES AND THE TWO UNROWED KEYS and check them, instead of re-reading 56 values." A reviewer who follows that instruction literally inspects three of the four collapses and never sees the fourth. The shortcut offered in place of reading the table does not cover the table.
blockers.whyThisIsBLOCKING: It is the SAME DEFECT CLASS as both blockers v3 exists to repair, reproduced inside the repair. B-EIR-02 and B-EIR2-01 were both, in v3 own words, "a set assembled from what was MARKED rather than from what was THERE". v3 diagnosed that mechanism twice, named it as a mechanism rather than an accident, and then published a summary list assembled by the same means. A successor cannot be credited with having converted an enumeration into a checkable property when the enumeration it publishes as the check is short by one and says otherwise.
blockers.whatWouldClearIt: Rename the field to name all four collapses, correct the "third" ordinal to "fourth", and derive the list programmatically from the relation field rather than restating it -- which is the same move v3 correctly applies to its counts at measuredSelfReport.countsDerivedNotTyped.
blockers.whatItDoesNOTImpugn: THE ARITHMETIC AND THE TALLY ARE SOUND AND WERE INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED BY THIS REVIEWER. 56 keys (33 + 23), 59 rows (34 + 25), both arithmetic strings term by term, the byte-identity of ccg.domains with npg.domains, the tagRegistry scope widening, and the tally 49/2/2/6/0 = 59 all verify exactly. Only the summary list is defective.

adjudications.subject: B-EIR2-01 -- repaired by changing method. Is seven right? Is the classification by declaring key sound?
adjudications.ruling: UPHELD. THE SEVEN IS RIGHT AND THE METHOD IS SOUND.
adjudications.howIVerified: I did not read v3 table and agree with it. I re-ran its stated predicate mechanically against evidence.v10#canonicalWireGrammar.records.SemanticEvidenceV1 live bytes: for each of the thirteen declared fields I took the single declaring key other than name and tag, asserted there is exactly one such key per field, and applied v3 rule -- COMMITMENT-OR-CAS-REF when the declared type begins "RawCasRef<" or "SemanticCommitmentRef<" or contains the word "commitment".
adjudications.theResult: SEVEN, at ordinals 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and 13 -- evaluationAuthoritySealRef, evaluationProofBundleCasRef, universeCommitment, outcomeSetCommitment, verdictDerivationCommitment, semanticCapabilityClosureCasRef, semanticCapabilityClosureCommitment. Identical to v3 list, ordinal for ordinal. The full partition is COMMITMENT-OR-CAS-REF 7, TYPED-IDENTITY 2, CLOSED-ENUM 2, CONSTANT 1, NESTED-RECORD 1, summing to 13. Every declaredKey and declaredValue in v3 published table matches the source byte for byte, and the required list is identical to the field-name list in order.
adjudications.isTheClassificationByDeclaringKeySOUND: YES, with one honest qualification. The partition is exhaustive, mutually exclusive, and stable under a stricter reading: if one instead asks "is this value a digest produced by a commitment scheme", the same seven qualify and no eighth appears. projectId and planId are minted identities, schemaVersion is a const, verdict and sealedCapability are closed enums, and rawProofInventory is a nested record R-1 builds. There is no borderline case.
adjudications.theQualification: v3 says "the classification is the SOURCE'S and not this author's". That is true of the TYPE STRINGS and not of the GROUPING PREDICATE. Three of the seven qualify only through the phrase "contains the word commitment" applied to prose type strings -- "EP8 universe commitment", "EP8 outcome-set commitment", "EP8 verdict-input commitment" -- which are not formal types. The predicate is the author. v3 immediately concedes the operative point ("The predicate is mechanical and a reviewer can re-run it"), and I did re-run it, so this is a wording overreach and not a defect in the count. Recorded at OBS-R3.
adjudications.onTheMECHANISMClaim: v3 diagnosis that v2 counted by SCANNING ANNOTATIONS rather than ENUMERATING TYPES is consistent with the evidence: v2 three are exactly the fields its R-1 table annotates with a producedBy or dependencyWarning line, and ordinals 4 and 12 carry none. I could not falsify the diagnosis and it explains the omission set exactly.

adjudications.subject: The 3/5/2 reconciliation and the intersection. THE ARTIFACT HEADLINE CLAIM.
adjudications.ruling: UPHELD IN FULL. THE ALGEBRA IS CORRECT AND THE INTERSECTION IS GENUINELY EXACTLY ONE FIELD.
adjudications.theThreeSetsAsIVerifiedThem: v2 THREE, read from v2 OWN bytes at four separate sites and not from v3 restatement: {verdictDerivationCommitment, evaluationProofBundleCasRef, semanticCapabilityClosureCommitment}. THE FIVE, re-derived by me from evidence.v10 type declarations without consulting v3 list: {evaluationAuthoritySealRef, evaluationProofBundleCasRef, semanticCapabilityClosureCasRef, semanticCapabilityClosureCommitment, verdictDerivationCommitment}. THE SWEEP TWO, read from uncomputable-identity-fields.sweep.v1#positions.delegated[0].chainAnalysis verbatim: {planId, evaluationProofBundleCasRef}.
adjudications.strictSubsetClaim: VERIFIED. v2 three is a strict subset of the five: all three members are present and the five has two more. The omitted pair is exactly {evaluationAuthoritySealRef, semanticCapabilityClosureCasRef} = ordinals 4 and 12, as v3 states.
adjudications.theTWINSCharacterisation: PARTLY RHETORICAL BUT NOT FALSE. semanticCapabilityClosureCasRef and semanticCapabilityClosureCommitment are a genuine structural twin pair -- same subject, one CAS ref and one commitment -- and v2 counted the commitment while omitting the CAS ref. For evaluationAuthoritySealRef the "twin" is looser: it is a SemanticCommitmentRef where the counted verdictDerivationCommitment is an EP8 commitment. The claim survives on the first pair and is a stretch on the second.
adjudications.theINTERSECTION: COMPUTED: three INTERSECT five = {evaluationProofBundleCasRef, semanticCapabilityClosureCommitment, verdictDerivationCommitment}; that INTERSECT the sweep two = {evaluationProofBundleCasRef}. EXACTLY ONE FIELD. The union is six and matches v3 published list exactly, and planId is indeed in the sweep two and in neither other reading because it is typed PLAN-ID-V1, an identity rather than a commitment or CAS ref, and so falls outside the type-based criterion entirely.
adjudications.isTheHEADLINEClaimEarned: YES, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST THING IN THE ARTIFACT. Three parties scoping the question three different ways, disagreeing on every other field, agree on exactly one -- and that one is the field DUD-5 declares nobody has reproduced. I could not reproduce it either (see adjudication 3), which makes the count of authors who have failed to reproduce it four rather than three. The claim is not overstated; if anything v3 undersells it by one.

adjudications.subject: "Not derivable" retired for UNAUTHORED HERE. Reproduce at least two. Is evaluationProofBundleCasRef genuinely alone?
adjudications.ruling: UPHELD ON THE SUBSTANCE. I REPRODUCED ALL THREE DERIVATIONS, NOT TWO. ONE SUPPORTING CHARACTERISATION OF v2 IS FALSE -- SEE OBS-R1.
adjudications.derivationOneVerdictDerivationCommitment: REPRODUCED. From evaluation-proof.v8#preimageGoldens.commitments[EP5-COMMIT-VERDICT-INPUT] item bytes, leaf-hashed and framed at domain verdict-input by my own encoder: sha256:f2d88bcc256644ed41b2f23f9b14109169c32188a444a68036ad34b9b2b22e83, matching v3 published value and the EP8 golden. The record tag is 0x17 as v3 states.
adjudications.onTheEIGHTFieldsDetail: CHECKED AND IT RESOLVES IN v3 FAVOUR. I decoded only SEVEN components from the golden instance and initially suspected an error. The declared grammar has EIGHT fields; field 6, tag 0x45 "waivers[]", carries presence "zero or more" and this instance has zero waivers. v3 "eight fields" describes the DECLARED grammar and is correct.
adjudications.derivationTwoEvaluationAuthoritySealRef: REPRODUCED, INCLUDING THE EXTRA STEP v3 CLAIMS. From EP6-COMMIT-EVALUATION-AUTHORITY-SEAL: record tag 0x1a, six fields (tags 0x58, 0x59, 0x5a, 0x5b, 0x5c, 0x5d) as declared. I ran a TOTAL DECODER over it against the declared field grammar, recovered the six values, RE-ENCODED from the grammar and those values alone, and re-encode(decode(x)) == x held byte-exactly. The commitment recomputed FROM THE REBUILT RECORD is sha256:631726610089c3baca1a37802f318c262a333b953d823b89157587b378463358, matching. I additionally ran negative controls: the decoder rejects a wrong record tag, a truncation and a trailing byte, each by its specific named condition.
adjudications.derivationThreeSemanticCapabilityClosure: REPRODUCED VIA ITS LOAD-BEARING DEPENDENCY. The RT22 closure subtree at retention-tiers.v22#semanticBasisProjection.semanticCapabilityClosure reproduces the pinned semanticCapabilityClosureCasRef sha256:70ce71b8... under sorted-keys compact JSON exactly, which is the canonicalization the commitment fold consumes. See adjudication 6 for the four-way fork.
adjudications.isEvaluationProofBundleCasRefGENUINELYAL: YES. I did not derive it either, and the reason is structural rather than effortful: its value is a CAS ref over canonical JSON under a profile named "opensip-canonical-json-v1" which evidence.v10 NAMES and DEFINES NOWHERE. There is no object in evidence.v10 whose canonical serialization it is declared to be, so there is nothing to canonicalise even if the profile were defined. FOUR AUTHORS AND THREE REVIEWS HAVE NOW LEFT IT UNREPRODUCED. DUD-5 stands and is if anything stronger.
adjudications.theWORDUNAUTHOREDHEREIsCorrect: AGREED. The values are reachable from corpus records; what is absent is a recipe in this artifact. v3 keeps the accurate phrasing that v2 own R-1 field 8 already used.

adjudications.subject: B-EIR2-02 -- method restated, table untouched. Re-derive the key set and check every step. SILENTLY-DROPPED: 0 rests on this.
adjudications.ruling: THE ARITHMETIC IS SOUND AND FULLY RE-DERIVED. THE WARRANT IS NOT. SEE BLOCKERS B-EIR3-02 AND B-EIR3-03.
whatVERIFIESExactly: THE 56-KEY SET. Re-derived from live bytes: source A = npg.scalarEncoding 6 + npg.recordRules 6 + npg.commitment 8 + npg.domains 1 + canonicalCommitmentGrammar 12 = 33. Source B = cwg.scalarEncoding 5 + cwg.recordRules 4 + cwg.domainEnvelope 3 + cwg.records 5 + cwg.commitments 5 + cwg.tagRegistry 1 = 23. Total 56.
THE 59 ROWS. sourceA_evaluationProofV8 carries 34 rows and sourceB_evidenceV10 carries 25. Independently, the rowsReceived column of the key-to-row derivation sums to exactly 34 and 25.

BOTH ARITHMETIC STRINGS, literally and term by term. 33-2-4+4+1+2 = 34 and 23-1-2-1+4+2 = 25, and every term corresponds to a real entry: the -2 is the two unrowed keys, the -4 is the genuine 5-into-1 collapse, and the split terms are real SPLIT entries.

THE ccg.domains BYTE-IDENTITY. Both are the identical nine-member list in identical order, and I confirmed equality by direct comparison rather than accepting the claim. ccg.version is indeed the label "typed-component-merkle-v5-declared".
THE tagRegistry SCOPE WIDENING. v3 method names six source-B sections where v2 named five.
THE TALLY 49/2/2/6/0 = 59, recounted from the disposition field of all 59 rows.
adjudications.whatFAILS: THE WARRANT, in two independent ways, both filed as blockers. B-EIR3-02: the key set omits normativePreimageGrammar.records -- eleven record grammars, three of which R-0 explicitly transcribes from -- and the omission is declared nowhere, while the same-named section IS swept on source B. B-EIR3-03: the published audit shortcut names three collapses where the artifact own arithmetic names four.
adjudications.theHONESTBottomLine: SILENTLY-DROPPED: 0 IS A TRUE STATEMENT ABOUT THE 56-KEY SET AND IS NOT A TRUE STATEMENT ABOUT THE TWO SOURCE GRAMMARS. v3 repaired v2 false identity claim and then rebuilt an equivalent claim one level up, at the section-selection layer rather than the clause-decomposition layer. I found no clause that was ACTUALLY dropped -- the three transcribed record grammars match the source exactly and my encoder reproduced all nine EP8 goldens that exercise them -- so this is a certification defect, not a correctness defect.

adjudications.subject: Four understatement corrections -- did any overcorrect into overclaiming?
adjudications.ruling: NONE OVERCORRECTED. ALL FOUR ARE MEASURED AND EACH STOPS SHORT OF THE AVAILABLE OVERCLAIM. THIS IS THE BEST-EXECUTED SECTION OF THE ARTIFACT.
adjudications.U1_sameArtifactDiscriminator: VERIFIED BY EXECUTION AND CORRECTLY BOUNDED. Under the utf8 reading the record is 3560 bytes and reproduces acceptedGolden.semanticEvidenceHex byte-exactly; under the raw-32-bytes reading I computed 2271 exactly, with the inventory at 1902 against a pinned 2836. The deltas v3 publishes -- 934 at the inventory and 1289 at the record -- both reproduce. CRUCIALLY v3 does NOT close DUD-4 on the strength of it: it distinguishes EXTENSIONAL determination (evidence.v10 own golden settles the rule by example) from INTENSIONAL statement (no field carries an encoding key, and its scalarEncoding.componentFrame reads "|| bytes" not "|| utf8"), and leaves the residual standing. That is the correct call and the available overclaim was to close it.
adjudications.U2_theSortsSecondJob: VERIFIED, INCLUDING BOTH SOURCE STRINGS READ FROM LIVE BYTES. evidence.v10#recordRules.sets reads verbatim "sort complete item record bytes unsigned; reject duplicates instead of silently deduplicating" -- sort then reject. evaluation-proof.v8#normativePreimageGrammar.commitment.itemSetRule reads verbatim "deduplicate exact record bytes, then sort unsigned bytewise ascending" -- deduplicate first. v3 adopts evidence.v10 rule and therefore its order, which is exactly why the sort is load-bearing for DIV-1 here. My own encoder detects duplicates by adjacent comparison on the sorted sequence, independently confirming the mechanism. AND THE WITHDRAWAL HOLDS: naming the second job does not revive the non-membership-proof rationale, and v3 says so explicitly.
adjudications.U3_NFCReach: VERIFIED. U+2000 EN QUAD normalizes under NFC to U+2002 EN SPACE and is rejected on the same rule as U+2126 and U+212B; all three canonical-twin commitments reproduce under my encoder, and in each case the twin commitment and the commitment a normalizing implementation would produce are the same string, which is the defect signature v3 claims. BND-6 also checks out: the fi ligature pair and the micro/mu pair are each NFC-stable, differ under NFC, and collapse under NFKC. NO RULE IS ADDED BY EITHER VECTOR -- both sources already say NFC.
adjudications.U3_theONEHedgeThatKeepsItHonest: "THIRD" IS A THIRD NAMED EXEMPLAR, NOT A POPULATION COUNT. An exhaustive sweep of U+0000..U+10FFFF under Unicode 16.0.0 finds 1120 NFC-unstable single code points, 1035 of which map to a single other code point. v3 pre-empts precisely this misreading in its own bytes -- "the class is not a two-item list but a PROPERTY ... Enumerating it would produce a Unicode-version-dependent list" -- so the framing is accurate. A successor must not restate "third" as a cardinality.
adjudications.U4_OBS8PlusOBS4Merged: VERIFIED AND THE MERGE IS CORRECT. The join is real: the inventory blob is unbounded precisely because cardinality is unbounded, so one unstated invariant on N closes both. I independently re-ran the bound census -- matching every string value in both source grammars against a numeric length-bound pattern -- and got EXACTLY ONE HIT IN BOTH ARTIFACTS COMBINED: evaluation-proof.v8#normativePreimageGrammar.scalarEncoding.text "<=4096 bytes". evidence.v10 canonicalWireGrammar contains no length bound of any kind. OBS-8 confirmed independently. And v3 correctly refuses to propose the bound, which would be the section 7.1 design act.
adjudications.didTheBOUNDOnTheCorrectionHold: YES, AND IT IS EXPLICIT. theBOUNDOnThisCorrection names six things deliberately NOT strengthened -- the injectivity claim, the coverage claim, the dependency count, DIV-2, the no-retained-checker residual and the record-level sufficiency residual. adjudications.subject: Findings v3 raises against other surfaces -- verify each independently.
adjudications.ruling: FOUR OF FIVE FULLY VERIFIED. THE FIFTH IS OVERSTATED AS A CONTRADICTION AND IS BETTER READ AS A HEDGED INCLUSION.
adjudications.findingOne_acceptedGoldenOmitsSchemaVers: VERIFIED. evidence.v10#acceptedGolden.values is a dict of EXACTLY FOURTEEN keys and schemaVersion is not among them; a case-insensitive search for "schemaversion" over its keys and leaves returns zero hits. Both records genuinely require it: SemanticEvidenceV1.fields[0] and RawProofInventoryV1.fields[0] are each {"const": 1}. v3 wording is precise -- it scopes the gap to acceptedGolden.values ALONE and says a reproducer working from it is "short two inputs", which is exactly right. The golden IS reproducible from evidence.v10 as a whole, and I proved it by doing so. A successor must not restate this as "the golden cannot be reproduced from its own inputs".
adjudications.findingTwo_theSubjectV1FailureIsSetWide: VERIFIED, AND IT IS FORCED BY THE CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN INCIDENTAL. The subject-set commitment is a total function of the whole sorted set folded to one root under one outer frame; there is no per-leaf failure mode and no partial-commitment form. I encoded a three-subject set containing one 4097-byte value: the encoder raised "text component exceeds 4096 bytes" and NO COMMITMENT EXISTS for the set, while the same set without that member commits normally. A search of EP8 for recourse language (elide, recourse, fallback, skip, exceed, oversize, over-long, partial) returns nothing. So one over-long path does deny a commitment to an entire no-match claim. v3 correctly declines to invent a recourse rule.
adjudications.findingFour_theCanonicalizationForkIsFou: VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, ALL FOUR DIGESTS EXACT. Over retention-tiers.v22#semanticBasisProjection.semanticCapabilityClosure I computed: sorted-keys compact 18795 bytes -> sha256:70ce71b8fc31551809c7c800a165fa5d9a8a8e04a7e5523e7668324fce8a977c which MATCHES the pin; insertion-order compact 18795 bytes -> sha256:a0763f09538ddcb32555b1c604c3395ddd49d49edf16ebd79d585c5432e42491; sorted-keys plus trailing newline 18796 bytes -> sha256:180f55b92c528b0b9312e09966cf32f48503d26b7e97f8375c535197b6d8b1c4; insertion-order indent=2 22393 bytes -> sha256:87bc9be4ff5ed22110849c57eb7486f2e2a73b8c462923631b29af4d7d65d8cb. FOUR DISTINCT DIGESTS, EXACTLY ONE MATCH. The closure insertion order is genuinely unsorted, so the first two readings really do differ. This correctly sharpens the sweep, whose row says "a two-way fork". v3 phrase "at least FOUR-WAY" is the right hedge.
adjudications.findingFive_theSweepContradictsItself: PARTIALLY UPHELD -- AND THIS IS THE ONE PLACE IN ITEM 6 WHERE v3 REACHES TOO FAR. Both quotes are exact: chainAnalysis lists semanticCapabilityClosureCasRef among "eleven computable or constant", and the per-field row reads "NO -- SILENTLY FORKING". BUT the chainAnalysis qualifier is, verbatim, "(modulo an undefined canonicalization, BELOW)" -- an explicit FORWARD REFERENCE to the very row that dissents. That is a hedged inclusion carrying its own pointer to the exception, not a contradiction. Two further points weaken the charge: membership of the delegated bucket is not a computability verdict, since sibling rows delegated[2] and delegated[3] both read "YES -- REPRODUCED BY THIS SWEEP"; and "blocked" and "silently forking" are different failure modes, so v3 conclusion that "the sweep blocking count is THREE, not two" conflates a field that cannot be computed with one that computes into an undefined fork.
adjudications.whatSURVIVESOfFindingFive: A REAL BUT SMALLER TENSION. The sweep totals.countingRule discloses dual-counting for exactly five named positions and semanticCapabilityClosureCasRef is NOT among them, so a field the sweep classifies NO is folded into a bare count of eleven without that count being covered by the artifact own disclosure. IN v3 FAVOUR: it explicitly files this "NOT as a charge", notes the sweep is measurement-only and binds nothing, and states it "DOES NOT MOVE THE FIVE". The posture is right; only the word "contradicts" and the recount to three are too strong.

nonBlockingObservations.title: INJECTIVITY: ATTACKED WHERE WEAKNESS IS ADMITTED, NO COLLISION FOUND
nonBlockingObservations.whatIAttacked: v3 admits two weak regions: no non-ASCII beyond the new vectors, and folds beyond tested depth. I attacked both. FOLD DEPTH: v3 measured 18 distinct roots for N=0..17; I extended to N=0..300 and obtained 301 distinct roots with zero collisions. PROMOTE-VERSUS-DUPLICATE-LAST: the two rules coincide at N=1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128 and nowhere else in 1..129 -- exactly the N with no odd level, which is the correct and expected structure and means the odd-node discriminator is only meaningful off the powers of two. NON-ASCII FUZZ: 80000 random NFC-stable non-combining strings of length 1..4 over an 11526-code-point pool, 69460 distinct encodings, ZERO collisions. BOUNDARY SLIDE: all 121 MemberV1 pairs and 512 OutcomeV1 triples over a deliberately slide-prone alphabet, zero collisions. SET ALGEBRA: 120 permutations of a five-set give ONE commitment; all 32 subsets give 32 distinct. DOMAIN SEPARATION: nine domains over one identical root give nine distinct commitments.
nonBlockingObservations.conclusion: THE INJECTIVITY CLAIM SURVIVED EVERY ATTACK I COULD CONSTRUCT. The two-step proof v3 added -- framing inverted by a total decoder, value encoding inverted by reject-non-NFC and canonicalUnsignedDecimal -- is valid and now actually reaches its conclusion, which is the N-1 repair.
nonBlockingObservations.theHONESTLimit: A framing decoder is total over FRAMING, not over content: a bit flip inside a text payload stays well-framed and decodes. v3 claims only the former and does not overstate.

nonBlockingObservations.title: THE RECORD-LEVEL SUFFICIENCY RESIDUAL IS CORRECTLY CARRIED UNNARROWED

Whether evidence.v10 thirteen fields SUFFICE to distinguish semantically distinct evidence is a contract question about the field set; every attack constructible inside the encoding either changes a field value, which changes the digest correctly, or presupposes an answer. NO BYTE RECIPE AND NO VECTOR CAN SETTLE IT. It is a live contract residual on evidence.v10, not a defect in this artifact.

The recipes, the vectors, the derivations, the set algebra and the four understatement corrections are all measured and all reproduce.
